skill_name: Compare and contrast an open-source and a proprietary software.
workflow: Open-source and proprietary software have many differences. Open-source software is available to view, edit and use by anyone with permission, and the code is distributed freely. Proprietary software is owned by the creator, and the code is kept secret. Open-source software is often developed by volunteers and supported by the open-source community, but proprietary software is developed and supported by the company owning the code. Open-source software has no costs associated with it and updates
